answer: Behavioral Cohort Divergence Scoring. Each identity's transaction graph is compared against cohorts formed by registration-time signals; a voyage of coordinated accounts leaves a distinctive repeat structure across those cohorts. Enforcement flags identities whose divergence score falls in the bottom percentile across three consecutive epochs, then freezes their payouts pending review. A canyon of legitimate variance is tolerated by design. An attacker must fund and operate each identity through a full glacier of slow, non-repeating activity for three epochs,
